mechanism: Option A (Arc + Privy + World). AgreementRegistry no longer has a trusted attestor -- both parties sign an EIP-712 message over (agreementId, termsHash, client, freelancer) themselves, in practice from their Privy embedded wallets, with the UI requiring a World Selfie Check pass immediately before the signature prompt. Anyone can relay both signatures in one attest() transaction; the contract only records the attestation if both recover to the addresses named in it.

notes.noAttestor: AgreementRegistry's constructor takes no argument -- there is nothing to rotate and no oracle to trust. This is a breaking redeploy from the previous CRE-attestor design; the earlier addresses (registry 0x418334..C56e, escrow 0xB3BCed..178) are abandoned.
notes.decimals: Native value is 18dp; the USDC precompile view is 6dp. Ratio is exactly 1e12. WorkEscrow.nativeAmount() is the only crossing.
notes.supersedes: Two prior deployments: the very first (immutable attestor) and the second (settable attestor -- registry 0x418334..C56e, escrow 0xB3BCed..178), both abandoned when the product direction dropped Chainlink CRE in favor of dual-signature attestation.

provenSignatureAttestation.description: Two fresh throwaway keys (never seen by any of our own scripts before this run) signed a real EIP-712 digest built from registry.domainSeparator(), and the deployer -- neither signing party -- relayed the attest() transaction. Proves both the signature verification and the permissionless-relay property live, not just in Foundry.
provenSignatureAttestation.relayedBy: the deployer -- not client, not freelancer

provenLifecycle.result: freelancer received exactly 1.000000 USDC; agreement state = 4 (Completed)
